before_step.derivation: From step 1, a decision state is (x,y,s,k,vP,vQ) with x,y in 0..9, s in {start,R,D} the last move, k in {0,1,2} its run length, and vP,vQ checkpoint flags. Define the transition relation T on this state by a labeled move m in {R,D}. Legality conditions: (i) run-length legality: it is not the case that s=m and k=2, so a third consecutive identical move is forbidden. (ii) Grid legality: the resulting cell (x',y') must satisfy x'<=9 and y'<=9; concretely, on R set (x',y')=(x+1,y) and require x<9; on D set (x',y')=(x,y+1) and require y<9. (iii) Forbidden cells: the new cell (x',y') must not lie in F={(2,2),(4,3),(5,6),(7,5),(8,8)}; otherwise the branch is discarded. If legal, update: s'=m; k'=1 if m differs from s, else k+1 (which by (i) is at most 2); vP'=vP or ((x',y')==(3,4)); vQ'=vQ or ((x',y')==(6,7)). Thus the transition is (x,y,s,k,vP,vQ) --m--> (x',y',s',k',vP',vQ') with m in {R,D}, subject to (i)-(iii). Illegal moves have no successor (the relation admits no such edge). This relation is exactly the per-move stepping needed for counting and lexicographic search in later steps.
before_step.result: Transition T: state (x,y,s,k,vP,vQ) has an edge labeled R iff x<9, not(s=R and k=2), and (x+1,y) is not in F; then x'=x+1, y'=y, s'=R, k'=k+1 if s=R else 1, vP'=vP or (x',y')=(3,4), vQ'=vQ or (x',y')=(6,7). Edge labeled D iff y<9, not(s=D and k=2), and (x,y+1) not in F; then y'=y+1, x'=x, s'=D, k'=k+1 if s=D else 1, same flag updates with (x',y'). Illegal moves yield no successor.
